sources.title: Don't blame it on ethnicity: The role of group identities and climate risks in farmer-herder relations in Senegal
sources.organization: Journal of Peace Research; Wageningen University & Research
geographic_coverage: Ferlo Desert silvopastoral zone in Louga Region
sources.temporal_coverage: Field data collected October-November 2022; article published November 2025.
sources.methodology: Mixed-method public-good experiment plus 14 focus groups; abstract reports 332 participants, while Methods reports 337.
sources.limitations: Publisher full text was inaccessible; abstract and Methods give conflicting sample totals. Game behavior is not observed conflict.

sources.title: Senegal, Evaluation of Green Climate Fund Project: 2020-2024
sources.temporal_coverage: R4 project implementation 2020-01-14 to 2024-10-14; evaluation conducted July 2024-February 2025.
sources.methodology: WFP publisher summary of a decentralized, end-of-project evaluation; full evaluation methods were not accessible.
sources.limitations: The publisher summary omits design details, sample, subgroup estimates and effect sizes; the linked evaluation PDF required JavaScript verification.

sources.title: Strengthening adaptive and socio-economic capacities of women and youth in the village of Mbam through the Integrated Resilience Garden approach
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), SAGA 2
sources.temporal_coverage: Project page lists start date 2024-09-06 and end date 2026-05-31, while still displaying status as active.
sources.methodology: Official FAO project page describing local objectives, implementation partners and listed activities.
sources.limitations: The page's displayed active status conflicts with its May 2026 end date; listed activities are not independently verified as completed outcomes.

sources.title: Challenges to food security in a changing environment: a community-based participatory research study in Casamance, Senegal (West Africa)
sources.temporal_coverage: Study field period not stated in the article; published 2026-03-31.
sources.methodology: Mixed-method participatory study: 42 exploratory participants, then 234 agricultural interviewees across 13 communities.
sources.limitations: Purposive sample from selected communities; partly self-reported and cross-sectional, limiting generalization.

claims.locator: Article section 'The case of farmers and herders in Senegal.'
claims.paraphrase: The study compared Groundnut Basin farmers with Ferlo/Louga agro-pastoralists, linked by seasonal southward herd migration; Ferlo has a long dry season and contested pasture.
claims.limitations: The two municipalities are unnamed; study is not nationally representative.

claims.locator: Article Abstract; Results sections on out-group cooperation and collective risk; Discussion.
claims.paraphrase: Out-group priming reduced cooperation, especially among farmers; focus groups linked distrust to stereotypes of mobile herders. The collective-risk treatment widened the in-group/out-group cooperation gap.
claims.scenario: Collective-risk treatment was a climate-risk analogue, not a modeled scenario.
claims.limitations: Treatment simulated rather than observed climate risk; results are game cooperation, not violence. Risk did not significantly lower out-group cooperation.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Authors say climate-related collective risks may widen group bias and raise conflict-escalation risks.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Article Abstract; Results sections on collective risk; Discussion.

claims.locator: Publisher summary, project description and reach; paragraphs on evaluation findings.
claims.paraphrase: The R4 initiative targeted 405,000 people across Kolda, Tambacounda, Kaffrine, Fatick and Kaolack through adaptation assets, agricultural insurance, savings/income support and government risk management; reported reach was 438,291.
claims.limitations: Reported reach is project coverage, not a measured resilience outcome.

claims.locator: Publisher summary, key evaluation findings under Efficiency and Impact & Innovation.
claims.paraphrase: The evaluation summary reports gains in food security, savings, insurance uptake, social cohesion, economic resilience and natural-resource management, while transfer delays, weak monitoring and staff turnover hindered delivery.
claims.limitations: The accessible summary provides no effect sizes or counterfactual; results are evaluation-reported, not independently re-estimated here.

claims.locator: Publisher summary, Gender & Inclusion and Sustainability findings.
claims.paraphrase: Women were active in savings groups but had limited access to unsubsidized insurance; youth and people with disabilities were under-targeted, and community structures had weak government anchoring and insurance literacy.
geographies: Five R4 target regions in Senegal
claims.limitations: Findings are available only in the publisher's condensed summary; group-specific denominators are not given.

claims.locator: Project page, objective/goal and area of intervention; activity 1.
claims.paraphrase: FAO lists a community-led garden in Mbam, Oudalaye commune, Matam Region, intended to strengthen food security, climate resilience and livelihoods for women and youth; the page lists over 200 participants and local-authority involvement.
institutions: Fédération des Associations du Fouta pour le Développement
claims.limitations: The page does not provide a participant breakdown or verify completed project outcomes; its active status conflicts with the listed May 2026 end date.

claims.paraphrase: Listed activities include three hectares for horticulture and agroforestry, water supply and farm inputs, climate-adaptation training, and an incubator for ten agri-entrepreneurs with an income platform for women and youth.
institutions: Fédération des Associations du Fouta pour le Développement
claims.limitations: The page presents activities and intended outputs; it does not confirm which were completed by the stated project end date.

claims.locator: Abstract; Results, Participant characteristics and Table 2.
claims.paraphrase: Across 13 Basse-Casamance communities, 234 agricultural participants reported irregular rainfall and environmental change; 86% had food-access difficulty, and all linked change to food insecurity.
claims.limitations: Selected communities and self-reported experience limit national generalization; field period is not stated.

claims.locator: Introduction subsection 'Casamance, changing environment, and food security background'; Results, Table 2 and Theme 5 'Abandonment of the land.'
claims.paraphrase: Participants said conflict (99.1%) and displacement (97.8%) affected food security; the article cites landmines and displacement constraining land access and production, with about 80% of farmland unusable.
institutions: Movement of Democratic Forces of Casamance
claims.limitations: The 80% landmine estimate is cited context, not survey measurement; percentages are respondents' reports.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: Authors say conflict and displacement restrict land and production, intersecting with environmental pressures.
claims.source_stated_fcv_locator: Introduction subsection 'Casamance, changing environment, and food security background'; Results, Theme 5 'Abandonment of the land.'

claims.locator: Abstract; Results, Theme 6 'Community-proposed solutions'; Discussion, 'Resilience and local food systems.'
claims.paraphrase: Participants proposed reforestation, sustainable farming and stronger environmental agencies; authors highlight women's roles in horticulture, seed management and local food-system resilience.
institutions: Ministry of Environment and Sustainable Development
claims.limitations: Proposals and discussed mechanisms are not evaluated interventions or measured resilience outcomes.

search_audit.query: Senegal climate change named region district community vulnerability rainfall drought food insecurity agriculture primary study
search_audit.outcome: Found original community research in Basse-Casamance and Groundnut Basin/Ferlo study sites, plus district/region-specific resilience evidence from WFP and FAO. Exact names for some sampled communities or municipalities are not provided.

search_audit.query: Senegal farmer herder climate collective risk conflict cooperation stereotypes original research
search_audit.outcome: Found a mixed-method experiment linking collective-risk conditions with wider in-group/out-group cooperation differences and focus-group accounts of mistrust and stereotypes; this is not evidence that climate shocks caused observed violence.

search_audit.query: Senegal Casamance conflict displacement landmines land access agriculture environmental pressure adaptation evidence
search_audit.outcome: Found Casamance evidence that conflict and displacement constrain land access and agricultural production and intersect with environmental pressures on food systems. No located source established that insecurity prevented a specific adaptation project from operating.

search_audit.query: Senegal climate resilience community adaptation project evaluation local institutions women farmers report
search_audit.outcome: Found WFP's R4 evaluation summary across five regions and FAO's named-site Mbam garden project; WFP provides evaluation-reported outcomes, while FAO's page chiefly lists objectives and activities with inconsistent status dates.

gaps: The Senegal-specific climate/FCV evidence located is bounded: the farmer-herder study uses a collective-risk experiment rather than real climate events, and the Casamance article reports conflict and displacement impacts on land and food systems rather than a measured climate-caused conflict pathway.
Conflict constrained agricultural land access and production in Casamance, but the targeted search did not establish that conflict or insecurity blocked a named adaptation delivery operation.
The WFP evaluation PDF was inaccessible behind JavaScript verification; findings here rely on the publisher summary, which omits methods, effect sizes and subgroup denominators.
The FAO Mbam project page still says active despite its listed 31 May 2026 end date; activity completion and outcomes remain unresolved.
The farmer-herder paper's publisher-indexed abstract and Methods section give different participant totals (332 and 337); claims avoid relying on the denominator.
Several research locations are described as zones or unnamed municipalities; no village-level identification is inferred beyond named Mbam and the Casamance study region.
